sections.html:
An Ohio eviction typically runs four to six weeks, so a tenant's belongings do not get set out the next day. After the landlord files, the court sends a summons and the hearing usually falls about two weeks later.

Cold weather does not pause the case, and a tenant can be evicted in winter. If you plan to sell, remember that the four to six weeks start only after the written notice has run. The full calendar from notice to an empty house is longer than the court phase alone.

sections.h2: Steps in an Ohio eviction case
sections.html:
Chapter 1923 of the Revised Code, the forcible entry and detainer chapter, sets the order of events. Each step leads to the next, and a landlord who skips one risks dismissal.

  • Written notice to leave, given at least three days before the case begins (R.C. 1923.04).
  • Complaint filed with the municipal or county court that covers the rental address.
  • Summons issued and served, at least seven days before trial (R.C. 1923.06).
  • Hearing before a judge unless a jury is demanded or the case is continued (R.C. 1923.09).
  • Judgment for restitution of the premises plus court costs.
  • Writ of execution requested and carried out by the sheriff, a police officer, a constable or a court bailiff (R.C. 1923.13 and 1923.14).
Ohio eviction stages and timing
StageTiming
Notice to leave (R.C. 1923.04)Three or more days before filing
Service of summons (R.C. 1923.06(A))At least seven days before the trial date
Hearing on possession (R.C. 1923.06(H))No sooner than the seventh day after service is complete
Answer to extra money claims (R.C. 1923.06(H))Twenty-eight days after service is complete
Officer carries out the writ (R.C. 1923.14(A))Within ten days after receiving it

The clerk always mails the summons and a copy of the complaint by ordinary mail with a certificate of mailing. When filing, the plaintiff chooses a second method: service by a sheriff, a court bailiff or an adult the court designates, or certified mail with return receipt.

The person serving goes to the rental. If the tenant is home, the papers are handed over. If not, they are left with someone of suitable age and discretion at the address. If neither works, a copy is posted in a conspicuous place on the premises. The server must return the process to the clerk within five days and note the method used.

Service is complete once the first two methods are done, or once ordinary mailing and posting have both happened. The summons also warns that a tenant depositing rent with the clerk must keep depositing it until the hearing, that a jury trial may be requested, and that free legal help may be available.

If no one asks for a jury or a continuance, a judge tries the case, and R.C. 1923.09 allows three outcomes.

  • Complaint true: judgment for restitution of the premises to the landlord, with costs of suit.
  • Complaint true in part: restitution for that part only, with costs divided as the judge sees fit.
  • Complaint not true: judgment against the landlord for costs.

R.C. 1923.081 lets the same trial cover the landlord's claims for past due rent and other damages, unless the court continues those claims for good cause. A tenant's request to file an answer, a counterclaim or to take discovery is good cause, and the case then runs like other civil cases. A tenant who needs time to find a lawyer can ask for a continuance, and any agreement reached before the hearing should be in writing and told to the judge.

sections.h2: The writ of eviction after judgment
sections.html:
After a judgment of restitution, the landlord asks the court to issue a writ of execution. A red tag goes up on the door telling the tenant how long remains to leave, generally five days. After that the landlord can ask the officer to set the tenant's things out.

Under R.C. 1923.14, the officer must carry out the writ within ten days after receiving it by restoring the landlord to possession. A tenant who appeals and gets a stay of execution, after posting any required bond, can pause the removal, and the judge then orders the officer to delay further proceedings.

sections.h2: Selling a rented house during an eviction
sections.html:
A pending case does not stop an owner from signing a purchase contract, but the buyer cannot take possession until the tenant leaves voluntarily or the writ is carried out. Buyers who want the house vacant often ask the seller to finish the court process first. Others buy with the tenant in place.

Ohio's self-help ban still applies while the sale is in progress. A landlord may not shut off utilities or lock the tenant out to speed things up (R.C. 5321.15), and a retaliatory possession action can be raised as a defense (R.C. 5321.02).

Manufactured home parks follow their own end steps. If an evicted resident leaves a home unoccupied for three days after judgment, the operator may give the titled owner written notice to remove it within fourteen days. A home worth more than three thousand dollars goes to a sheriff's sale within sixty days of the writ. A home worth three thousand dollars or less can have its title transferred to the plaintiff within thirty days, through the clerk of the common pleas title division.

If the buyer is paying cash and accepts the house as it stands, the closing date can be tied to the date the writ is carried out, so nobody waits on a lender's timetable while the court calendar runs.

sections.h2: Where to get help with an eviction case
sections.html: Start with the clerk of the court named on the summons. The clerk can explain local filing and hearing procedures but cannot give legal advice. Free legal aid is listed by county, and Akron, Cleveland, Columbus and Toledo have Right to Counsel programs for some tenants with low income. Owners with several rentals often hire a landlord attorney, because a missed deadline can force a restart of the notice and filing sequence. Keep a file with the lease, the rent ledger, the notice, proof of delivery and every court paper, since the judge and the buyer will both ask for them.

faqs.q: How many days does a tenant have to leave after an Ohio eviction judgment?
faqs.a: The posted red tag generally allows five days. After that the landlord can ask the sheriff or bailiff to carry out the writ, which the officer must execute within ten days after receiving it.

faqs.q: Can a landlord evict a tenant in the winter in Ohio?
faqs.a: Yes. Evictions can happen in winter or very cold weather. The case follows the same notice, hearing and writ steps as in any other season.

faqs.q: What is the earliest an Ohio eviction hearing can be held?
faqs.a: No sooner than the seventh day after service of the summons is complete, under R.C. 1923.06(H). Service must be made at least seven days before the day set for trial.

faqs.q: Can a landlord collect back rent in the same Ohio case?
faqs.a: Often yes. R.C. 1923.081 allows the trial to include claims for past due rent and other damages, unless the court continues those claims for good cause such as a tenant's request to answer or take discovery.

faqs.q: Does an eviction filing stop a sale of the house?
faqs.a: No. An owner can still sell, but possession depends on the tenant leaving or the writ being carried out. A buyer who wants a vacant house usually asks the seller to complete the court process before closing.
